pageCache.pageTitle: Redstart pupils get creative with sock monkeys - The Redstart Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redstart pupils get creative with sock monkeys
Year 6 pupils at Redstart Primary School have been putting their creativity to the test by making their very own sock monkeys as part of their learning about World War Two.
Using their vivid imaginations, the pupils experimented with a variety of designs, colours and styles to create a fantastic collection of unique sock monkey characters. Each creation showcased the children’s individuality, creativity and enthusiasm for the project.
The activity links to the wartime theme of ‘Make Do and Mend’, a British Government campaign introduced during World War Two to encourage people to make the most of existing clothes and materials, reduce waste and conserve valuable resources for the war effort.
Sock monkeys became popular during periods of economic hardship, including the Great Depression and wartime, when families often had to find creative ways to make toys using materials, they already had at home. Worn-out work socks could be transformed into homemade monkey dolls, giving new life to items that might otherwise have been thrown away.
A spokesperson for the academy said: “Pupils have done a fantastic job creating their own sock monkeys. It has been wonderful to see their imaginations come to life through such a hands-on activity.
“The project has helped bring their learning about World War Two to life, while showing them how people in the past made the most of the resources available to them.
“We are incredibly proud of the creativity, effort and enthusiasm they have shown.”
The project has provided pupils with an engaging way to explore an important aspect of wartime life, while developing their creative skills and understanding the value of reusing materials and reducing waste.

pageCache.pageTitle: EYFS curriculum - The Redstart Primary School
pageCache.text:
EYFS curriculum
The Foundation Stage
There are seven areas of learning that are used to plan every activity and experience for the children. The professionals teaching and supporting your child will make sure that the activities are suited to your child’s unique needs. Children in the Early Years learn by playing, exploring, being active and through creative and critical thinking which take place both indoors and outside.
We encourage children to develop within the three prime areas first: Communication and language; physical development and personal, social and emotional development. The prime areas are essential for your child’s healthy development and future learning. As children grow, the prime areas will help the to develop skills in four specific areas. These are: Literacy, mathematics, understanding the world and expressive arts and design. Further information about the Early Years Foundation Stage can be found on the Foundation Years website: http://www.foundationyears.org.uk/
Personal, social and emotional development
We provide experiences and support which will help children to develop a positive sense of themselves and of others: respect to others; social skills; and a disposition to learn.
Communication and language
Children will be provided with opportunities to use their skills in a range of situations to help develop competence in speaking and listening. All children’s language skills will be supported by Somerset Total Communication.
Physical Development
Children will engage in a variety of activities designed to help develop their co-ordination, control, manipulation and movements. Activities will be provided to help and support children in developing and understanding the importance of physical activity and being healthy.
The specific areas for essential skills and knowledge include:
Mathematics Children will be supported in developing their understanding of problem solving, shapes and numbers in a broad range of contexts in which they can explore, enjoy, learn and practise their skills.
Literacy Children will hear rhymes and stories every day and have access to a cosy book corner. There will be lots of opportunities for children to make marks and improve their fine motor skills.
Understanding the world Children will be supported in developing the knowledge, skills and understanding that will help them learn about the world. They will enjoy investigating, exploring and experimenting both indoors and outdoors with a wide range of materials.
Expressive arts and design Children will be provided with opportunities to develop their imagination through art, music, movement, dance, role-play and storytelling. They will be supported in sharing their own thoughts, ideas and feelings, so becoming confident to express themselves.
Give your child a chance to learn these positive lessons by working with the nursery staff to make the settling-in period as easy as possible.
Before children start nursery, we like to meet with both parent and child to find out more about you both. We will then discuss an appropriate induction for your child and anything you may wish to share with us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Redstart pupils embrace adventure on residential trip - The Redstart Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redstart pupils embrace adventure on residential trip
Pupils from Redstart Primary School had an unforgettable residential visit to Kilve Court Residential Centre in Somerset, where they embraced the great outdoors, challenged themselves and created lasting memories.
Set between the beautiful Quantock Hills and the Somerset coast, Kilve Court provided the perfect backdrop for adventure, teamwork and personal development.
Throughout their stay, pupils took part in a wide range of exciting activities designed to build confidence, resilience, teamwork and cooperation.
Among the highlights were abseiling, climbing, blindfolded obstacle courses, team-building exercises and a scenic three-mile hike through the stunning Somerset countryside. The group also enjoyed a walk to Kilve Beach, taking in the area’s beautiful coastal scenery.
The residential experience encouraged pupils to step outside their comfort zones, support one another and develop valuable life skills, all while having fun and making new friendships.
A spokesperson for Redstart Primary School said: “The residential visit to Kilve Court was a fantastic opportunity for our pupils to challenge themselves, try new activities and grow in confidence.
“We are incredibly proud of the way they supported one another, worked as a team and embraced every opportunity.
“The memories they have made and the skills they have developed will stay with them long after the trip.”

pageCache.text:
Redstart pupils step back in time to the Victorian era
Year 5 pupils at Redstart Primary School have stepped back in time by dressing up as Victorian children and discovering what life was like during the era.
The special learning experience gave pupils the opportunity to explore the past in an engaging and memorable way.
Dressed in Victorian-style clothing, the children immersed themselves in the period, learning about how people lived, what children wore and how everyday life differed from today.
Through their Victorian-themed activities, pupils developed their understanding of this important period in British history, bringing their classroom learning to life and encouraging curiosity about the past.
The day provided a fun and interactive way for children to deepen their historical knowledge while imagining what life might have been like for children growing up in Victorian times.
A spokesperson for Redstart Primary School said: “It was wonderful to see our Year 5 pupils embrace the Victorian era with such enthusiasm.
“Dressing up helped bring history to life and gave the children a fantastic opportunity to explore how life has changed over time.
“Experiences like this make learning memorable, engaging and enjoyable for everyone involved.”

pageCache.text:
Young artists create wildlife masterpieces
Budding artists from Year 1 at Redstart Primary School have created some fabulous wildlife-inspired artwork during a recent art lesson.
The pupils have been learning all about different animals and wildlife and have put their learning into practice by creating colourful and imaginative pieces of artwork.
The young artists painted giraffes, snakes, ducks, pigs and many more animals, with staff hugely impressed by their creativity and enthusiasm.
A spokesperson for the academy said: “Our Year 1 pupils have worked incredibly hard on their artwork and it has been wonderful to see their creativity shine through.
“They have shown great enthusiasm while learning about animals and wildlife, and we are incredibly proud of the fantastic creations they have produced.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School - The Redstart Primary School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
The role of Forest School
Forest School gives the children an opportunity to spend time outdoors learning in a completely different way to the conventional classroom model. Forest School celebrates the right of all children to play, as decreed by the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
Please see below to see how skills develop at Forest School.
Forest School progression
Click below for Forest School dates.
Forest School schedule Autumn 2026
Equipment
In order to take a full and active part in Forest School, children should come properly prepared. They will get muddy, and clothes might get grass-stained and torn, so we recommend old clothes that are not valuable!
Summer Forest School – warm and sunny…
Winter Forest School – cold and wet…
Light trousers/jeans
Long-sleeved hoody/jacket
Apply sun-cream at start of day
Hayfever sufferers – Take anti-histamine before coming to school
Old trainers or walking boots/shoes
Two pairs of socks when wearing welly boots
Gloves, hat and scarf if it is really cold
Several layers in the cold are better than one thick one
Alternative footwear for inside wear
Strappy tops/vest tops
Sandals, crocs, flip flops etc.
Canvas shoes or ballet pumps
Remember how changeable the weather can be. Even on a hot summer morning there is always the chance that it will cloud over and rain, so a light waterproof (pac-a-mac) is a good idea even in the summer.
An important part of Forest School is learning to cook over an open fire. Some of the things we cook include bread, pizzas, soups and hot chocolate. If children have food allergies, it is very helpful if parents/carers can send in a box of alternative foods/drinks that you know are safe for your child to cook as an alternative. For example, an appropriate dairy free milk or gluten free flour.

School Clubs
Wraparound Care and Extra-Curricular Clubs
At Redstart Primary School and Nursery, we offer a range of wraparound care options to support families before and after the school day, as well as a variety of extra-curricular clubs throughout the year.
Bookings and payments for Breakfast Club and Tea Club can be made online via MCAS. If you require login details or support accessing the system, please contact the school office.
To help us ensure appropriate staffing levels, Breakfast Club places should be booked by 3.00pm on the previous day. We aim to be as flexible as possible, but advance booking is essential.
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club provides a safe, welcoming, and well-supervised environment for children aged 3 to 11 years. Sessions run from 7.45am, allowing children to enjoy a healthy breakfast, take part in a range of activities, and prepare for the school day ahead.
Children in Nursery through to Year 4 are escorted to their classrooms at the end of the session, while pupils in Years 5 and 6 make their way independently.
Session Times and Charges
School Children
School Children with Sibling Discount (5%)
Nursery Children
Nursery Children with Sibling Discount (5%)
A 5% sibling discount is available when one or more siblings are booked into the same session. This applies to children attending both the school and nursery.
Important Information
All prices are subject to change.
Tea Club
Tea Club provides a safe and enjoyable after-school environment for children in Reception to Year 6. Children are offered a light snack and drink and can take part in a variety of activities, including arts and crafts, games, homework support, reading opportunities, and outdoor play.
Sessions run from 3.15pm to 5.30pm.
Session Times and Charges
School Children
School Children with Sibling Discount (5%)
A 5% sibling discount is available when one or more siblings are booked into the same session.
Nursery Tea Club
Nursery children can attend Tea Club until 4.15pm, Monday to Thursday. Sessions take place within the Nursery building and include a light snack and drink.
For collection, please use the main gate and select the Nursery option on the intercom screen. Children will be collected from the Nursery entrance.
Important Information
All prices are subject to change.
Extra-Curricular Clubs
At Redstart, we believe that extra-curricular activities provide valuable opportunities for children to develop new skills, pursue their interests, build friendships, and strengthen relationships with staff.
We offer a range of lunchtime and after-school clubs which change each term. Information about available clubs and details of how to apply are shared with parents at the start of each booking period. As places are often limited, we encourage families to apply via MCAS promptly.
Parents will be notified if their child has been allocated a place via MCAS.
If your child no longer wishes to attend a club, please inform the school or the member of staff running the club. Unless we have received notification from a parent or carer, we will expect your child to attend as normal and cannot release them early from a club session.
Should a club need to be cancelled unexpectedly, we will make every effort to notify families as soon as possible.

pageCache.text:
Chard Rugby Club brings fun to Redstart
It was scrum down at Redstart Primary School when Chard Rugby Club visited the school to put on a fantastic coaching session for pupils.
With enthusiastic coaches and great energy from the pupils, the session saw children take part in a variety of drills and exercises throughout the session.
From throwing and catching the ball to running with the ball and developing their rugby skills, pupils enjoyed an action-packed session.
The coaches praised the pupils for their great effort, enthusiasm and listening skills, making the session a brilliant opportunity for children to get active, try something new and engage with a local rugby club.
A spokesperson for the academy said: “It was fantastic to see our pupils getting involved with such enthusiasm.
“The coaches from Chard Rugby Club were brilliant at encouraging the children, and it was wonderful to see them developing new skills while having lots of fun.
“We are very grateful to the club for providing such a positive and memorable experience for our pupils.”

Welcome to the Nursery
Welcome to The Redstart Nursery School. We are proud to be part of The Redstart Primary School which, along with the Nursery School, has been judged by Ofsted as a Good school.
We offer a very high quality of education for three- and four-year-olds, equipping them with the skills they require for school and their lives ahead.
We run daily sessions from 9am to 12pm and 12pm to 3pm.
Breakfast club and Tea club is available to our Nursery School children and is bookable via MCAS. Further details are available on our website under our academy/school clubs.
We offer 30 hours of childcare. Contact the finance administrator for more details on nursery@rps.clf.uk.
If you would like to register your interest in our nursery, please see link to the expression of interest form below. The office admissions administrator with get back to you within five working days. We invite parents and children to attend a stay and play session upon application, these sessions will be organised in groups so there is an opportunity for parents to ask questions whilst the children play.
Your child’s details will be placed on our system and you will be contacted approximately six weeks prior to your preferred start date. You will then be required to pay any additional fees in advance of the child’s funding becoming available at the hourly rate at the time of signing up.
Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any questions.

The Cabot Learning Federation
A mature Multi-Academy Trust in the South West of England that promotes the delivery of excellent educational experiences for our pupils, improving their life chances.
Welcome to our Federation
The Cabot Learning Federation is a family of 36 schools in Bristol, Gloucestershire, South Gloucestershire, North Somerset and Somerset. We are a mature multi-academy trust (MAT) serving communities in the South West. We lead the Five Counties Teaching School Hubs Alliance and School-Centred Initial Teacher Training (SCITT) and the Boolean Maths Hub, professional development provisions delivered from our CLF Institute.
​Instinctively collaborative and ambitious, our trust supports 18,000 children and young people aged 2 to 19 in a diverse array of settings and more than 3,000 employees. Whether you are a school or MAT wishing to join our family, an educator looking for a new opportunity or a parent or young person who simply wants to find out more about us, welcome and we look forward to hearing from you.
